questionStem: What is the solution to the given equation?
coreQuestion: How do you solve a linear equation that has a fraction on one side?
steps: Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction: 5x + 3 = 2(x + 9) = 2x + 18.
Subtract 2x from both sides: 3x + 3 = 18.
Subtract 3, then divide by 3: 3x = 15, so x = 5.

choices.rationale: Multiplies only the left side by 2 and writes 5x + 3 = x + 9, which gives 4x = 6; checking x = 1.5 in the original gives 5.25 on the left and 10.5 on the right.
Writes 5x + 3 = 2x + 9 (the 2 is not applied to the 9), which gives x = 2; checking x = 2 gives 6.5 on the left and 11 on the right.
Clearing the fraction gives 5x + 3 = 2x + 18, so x = 5. Check: (25 + 3)/2 = 14 = 5 + 9.
Reaches 3x + 3 = 18 but adds 3 instead of subtracting it, getting 3x = 21; checking x = 7 gives 19 on the left and 16 on the right.

stimulus: A pump fills a storage tank at a constant rate of 18 liters per minute.
questionStem: At this rate, how many hours will it take the pump to deliver 3240 liters?
coreQuestion: How do you combine a rate with a unit conversion?
steps: Convert the volume to time in minutes by dividing by the rate: 3240 / 18 = 180 minutes.
Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60: 180 / 60 = 3 hours.
Check: 18 liters per minute for 3 hours is 18 · 180 = 3240 liters.

choices.rationale: 3240 / 18 = 180 minutes, and 180 / 60 = 3 hours.
3240 / 60 = 54 divides the liters by 60 instead of dividing by the rate; it is neither minutes nor hours.
180 is the time in minutes, but the question asks for hours.
3240 · 18 / 60 = 972 multiplies by the rate instead of dividing, so the units do not work out to a time.

stimulus: The equation (x + 5)² − (x − 3)² = px + q is true for all values of x, where p and q are constants.
questionStem: What is the value of p + q?
coreQuestion: How do you find the coefficients of an expression written as a difference of two squared binomials?
steps: Expand each square: (x + 5)² = x² + 10x + 25 and (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9.
Subtract, distributing the negative sign to every term: x² + 10x + 25 − x² + 6x − 9 = 16x + 16.
So p = 16 and q = 16, and p + q = 32.

commonErrors.why: Gives only p (or only q); the question asks for p + q.
Subtracts only the x² term of (x − 3)², getting 4x + 34 instead of 16x + 16, so p + q = 38.

stimulus: A hiker plans a 270-kilometer trek. She walks for x hours at 6 kilometers per hour and bikes for y hours at 15 kilometers per hour, so that 6x + 15y = 270. The graph of this equation in the xy-plane passes through the point (0, 18).
questionStem: Which statement is the best interpretation of the point (0, 18) in this context?
coreQuestion: How do you interpret a point on the graph of a linear equation in two variables in context?
steps: Substitute the point: 6(0) + 15(18) = 270, so the equation is satisfied.
The x-value is the walking time and the y-value is the biking time, so (0, 18) means 0 hours of walking and 18 hours of biking.
Check the distance: 15 · 18 = 270 kilometers, the whole trek.

choices.text: The hiker walks for 18 hours and does not bike.
choices.rationale: Swaps the variables: x is the walking time and y is the biking time, so x = 0 means no walking and y = 18 means 18 hours of biking.

choices.text: The hiker bikes for 18 hours and does not walk.
choices.rationale: With x = 0 and y = 18, she bikes 18 hours at 15 kilometers per hour and covers 15 · 18 = 270 kilometers, the entire trek.

choices.text: The hiker covers 18 kilometers by biking and none by walking.
choices.rationale: The y-value is a time in hours, not a distance; 18 hours of biking covers 270 kilometers, not 18.

choices.text: Each additional hour of walking requires 18 fewer hours of biking.
choices.rationale: Along the line, each additional hour of walking lowers the biking time by 6/15 = 0.4 hour, not 18 hours.

stimulus: A support cable runs from the top of a vertical pole to a point on level ground. The pole is perpendicular to the ground, and the cable makes an angle θ with the ground, where tan θ = 15/8. The cable is 51 meters long.
questionStem: How high above the ground, in meters, is the point where the cable meets the top of the pole?
coreQuestion: How do you use a tangent ratio to find the sides of a right triangle when the hypotenuse is known?
steps: Since tan θ = 15/8, the legs are in the ratio 15 : 8, and the hypotenuse is √(15² + 8²) = 17 in the same units.
So sin θ = 15/17.
The pole height is 51 · sin θ = 51 · 15/17 = 45 meters.

choices.rationale: 15 is the numerator of the ratio 15/8, but the actual legs are scaled up by a factor of 3 because 51 = 3 · 17.
51 · 8/17 = 24 is the horizontal distance along the ground (the cosine leg), not the height.
51 · 8/15 = 27.2 treats 8/15 as the sine, but sin θ = 15/17.
The legs are 3 · 15 = 45 and 3 · 8 = 24 with hypotenuse 3 · 17 = 51, so the height is 45 meters.

stimulus: For positive values of a and b, consider the expression (8a<sup>6</sup>/b<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup>.
questionStem: Which of the following is equivalent to the given expression?
coreQuestion: How do you simplify a power of a quotient with a fractional exponent?
steps: Apply the exponent 2/3 to each factor: 8<sup>2/3</sup> · (a<sup>6</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup> / (b<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup>.
8<sup>2/3</sup> = (∛8)² = 4, (a<sup>6</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup> = a<sup>4</sup>, and (b<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup> = b<sup>2</sup>.
The result is 4a<sup>4</sup>/b<sup>2</sup>.

choices.rationale: This is the cube root (power 1/3) of the expression, (8a<sup>6</sup>/b<sup>3</sup>)<sup>1/3</sup> = 2a<sup>2</sup>/b, not the 2/3 power.
Takes the cube root of 8 but forgets to square it: 8<sup>2/3</sup> is 4, not 2.
(∛8)² = 4, (a<sup>6</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup> = a<sup>4</sup>, (b<sup>3</sup>)<sup>2/3</sup> = b<sup>2</sup>, giving 4a<sup>4</sup>/b<sup>2</sup>.
Leaves b<sup>3</sup> unchanged in the denominator instead of raising it to the 2/3 power, which gives b<sup>2</sup>.

stimulus: The linear function g satisfies g(−2) = 9 and g(6) = −7.
questionStem: For what value of x does g(x) = 0?
coreQuestion: How do you find where a linear function equals zero from two of its values?

commonErrors.why: This is g(0), the y-intercept, not the x-value where g(x) = 0.
This is the slope of g, not the zero.

stimulus: A fitness center surveyed 160 of its members about the type of workout they prefer. The results, sorted by age group, are shown in the table.
questionStem: One member who prefers cardio is selected at random from the surveyed members. What is the probability that this member is 40 or older?
coreQuestion: How do you find a conditional probability when the sample is restricted to one column of a two-way table?
steps: Restrict to the cardio column: 36 + 49 = 85 members prefer cardio.
Of those 85, 49 are 40 or older.
The probability is 49/85.

choices.rationale: 49/160 uses all 160 surveyed members as the denominator, but the selection is restricted to members who prefer cardio.
70/160 = 7/16 is the probability that a random member is 40 or older, ignoring the cardio condition.
Only the 85 members who prefer cardio are possible, and 49 of them are 40 or older, so the probability is 49/85.
49/70 = 7/10 is the probability that a 40-or-older member prefers cardio, which reverses the condition.

stimulus: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 2x − 3 and g(x) = x² + 1.
questionStem: For what positive value of x does f(g(x)) = 49?
coreQuestion: How do you solve an equation that involves a composition of two functions?
steps: Substitute g(x) into f: f(g(x)) = 2(x² + 1) − 3 = 2x² − 1.
Set 2x² − 1 = 49, so 2x² = 50 and x² = 25.
The positive solution is x = 5.

choices.rationale: Solving only g(x) = 49 gives x² = 48, so x = 4√3, which ignores f.
x² = 25 is correct but x itself is the square root of 25, not 25.
Solving only f(x) = 49 gives x = 26, which ignores g.

stimulus: A youth league buys x basketballs at $24 each and y volleyballs at $18 each. The league can spend at most $360, must buy at least 15 balls in all, and must buy more volleyballs than basketballs.
questionStem: Which of the following ordered pairs (x, y) satisfies all of these conditions?
coreQuestion: How do you test candidate points against a system of inequalities from a context?
steps: Write the conditions: 24x + 18y ≤ 360, x + y ≥ 15, and y > x.
Test each pair against all three conditions.

choices.rationale: 24(4) + 18(16) = 384, which is more than $360.
2 + 12 = 14, which is fewer than 15 balls (the cost, $264, is within budget).
24(10) + 18(6) = 348 and 10 + 6 = 16 pass, but 6 volleyballs is not more than 10 basketballs.
24(6) + 18(12) = 360 is within budget, 6 + 12 = 18 is at least 15, and 12 > 6.

stimulus: In the xy-plane, the graphs of y = x² − 5 and y = 2x + 3 intersect at two points.
questionStem: What is the greater y-coordinate of the two points of intersection?
coreQuestion: How do you find the intersection points of a parabola and a line?
steps: Set the expressions equal: x² − 5 = 2x + 3, so x² − 2x − 8 = 0.
Factor: (x − 4)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 4 or x = −2.
Then y = 2(4) + 3 = 11 and y = 2(−2) + 3 = −1, so the greater y-coordinate is 11.

commonErrors.why: This is the x-coordinate of the point, not its y-coordinate.
This is the smaller y-coordinate, at x = −2.
